addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

<result>I have a complete picture of the pipeline. Here's my report.

## formats/components CSS transform pipeline

### 1. How the build works — entry points and transforms

**Package:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/package.json` (`@pantoken/components`). Scripts of note:
- `build` (via `vp run build`, defined in `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks.build`): runs, in order:
  1. `vp run @pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media#build`
  2. `node scripts/component-styles.ts`
  3. `node scripts/generate.ts`
  4. `node scripts/build-entries.ts`
  5. `vp pack` (rolldown-based, per `vite.config.ts` `pack`)
- `generate` task: just `component-styles.ts && generate.ts` (this is what docs:dev invokes).

**Authoring source of truth:** real `.css` files under `src/components/*.css`, `src/utilities/*.css`, `src/rules/*.css` (e.g. `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/billboard.css`). They carry:
- a `pfx-` class-prefix **sentinel** (`.pfx-billboard`, `.pfx-billboard.-clickable`) — defined in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/lib/sentinel.ts` (`SENTINEL = "pfx-"`).
- `@media (--theme-canvas)` etc. theme custom-media at-rules.
- `@scope` at-rules and `var(--instui-…)` token refs, both passed through verbatim.

**The transform steps:**

1. **`scripts/component-styles.ts`** (`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts`): reads each source `.css`, and for each of the three themes `["rebrand","canvas","canvasHighContrast"]` runs PostCSS with the single plugin `themeCustomMedia({ theme })`. It emits `src/generated/component-styles.ts` — a TS module of string consts: `billboardByTheme = { rebrand, canvas, canvasHighContrast }` plus `billboard = billboardByTheme.rebrand`. This is where **custom-media theme resolution** happens (see plugin below). Doc comments are retained (load-bearing for the CSS-API docs).

2. **Prefix / modifier rewriting** happens at record-build time, not in PostCSS. Each record wrapper (e.g. `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/billboard.ts`) imports `billboardByTheme` and does `raw.replaceAll(SENTINEL, p)` inside `defineComponent({ css: (p, options) => … })`. `p` comes from `ns(prefix)` in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/lib/helpers.ts` (`ns("instui")` → `"instui-"`, so `.pfx-billboard` → `.instui-billboard`; empty prefix → `.billboard`). The trailing dash in `pfx-` keeps `.-clickable` modifiers valid after the swap. `define.ts` (`/Users/dwahl/.../src/lib/define.ts`) then splits the leading doc comment, appends size-alias and deprecated-alias twins (`lib/aliases.ts`), and `wrap()`s the standalone sheet.

3. **`scripts/generate.ts`**: emits the shipped aggregate sheets into `generated/` — `base.css`, `components.css`, `fonts.css`, `prose.css`, `select.css`, `icons.css`, `utilities.css` — all with the default `instui` prefix. It also writes `src/generated/_records.css` (the `pfx`-prefixed sheet used only as the cssdoc `providers` source-lint index; gitignored, never shipped).

4. **`scripts/build-entries.ts`**: emits one `generated/<name>.css` per component (46+ files) for the per-component subpath exports. **Build-only** — deliberately excluded from `generate` so docs:dev hot-reload doesn't write 46 files and trigger a watcher loop.

5. **`vp pack`** (config in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/vite.config.ts`): bundles `src/index.ts` + every `generated/*.css` into `dist/` with CSS splitting + minify, `inject:false`. Entry list is built dynamically from `generated/*.css` minus the aggregate sheet names.

**The theme plugin** (Q3 detail): `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/plugins/postcss/theme-custom-media/src/index.ts` (`@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media`, export `themeCustomMedia`). It walks `@media` at-rules, expands `--theme-*` aliases (`--theme-canvas` → `(theme: canvas)`, plus `--theme-light/dark` combos), **prunes branches for non-target themes**, strips the matching `theme:` clause from kept queries, unwraps always-true theme-only wrappers, and removes `@custom-media --theme-*` declarations. It never touches `@scope` or resolves `var()`.

### 2. Multi-theme component stylesheet generation for the docs demos (commit b399069)

The shipped `components.css` is lowered to a single theme (rebrand), so its `@media (--theme-*)` overrides are pruned and the docs' runtime theme toggle (`<html data-pantoken-theme="…">`) can't bring them back. The docs generate their own multi-theme sheet:

- **`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts`** — `scopedComponentsCss(prefix="instui")`. Calls `componentsCss({ prefix, theme })` from `@pantoken/components` for each theme, emits the rebrand rules unscoped as the base, then **diffs** each of `["canvas","canvasHighContrast"]` against the base at PostCSS-node granularity; the theme-only extra rules get their selectors re-scoped under `:root[data-pantoken-theme="<theme>"]`. It throws if a theme-only delta is a non-`rule` at-rule (unsupported nesting).

- **`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/scripts/components-sheet.ts`** (new in this commit) — `writeComponentsSheet()` writes the result to **two outputs**:
  1. `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/.vitepress/theme/generated/components.css` — imported by the docs theme (`docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`, which the commit changed from importing `@pantoken/components/components.css` to `./generated/components.css`). Powers the inline CSS-API `@example` previews.
  2. `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/public/demos-assets/components.css` (copy) — loaded by the `/play` runner iframes via `demos.ts`'s `cssUrls`.

## How `vpr docs:dev` and the docs orchestrator work

### 1. What `vpr docs:dev` runs

`vpr` = `vp run` (vite-plus). There are two `docs:dev` scripts in play:

**Root `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/package.json`:**
```json
"docs:dev": "vp run @pantoken/demo#build && vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:dev"
```
It first builds the demo runner, then delegates to the docs package.

**`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/package.json`:**
```json
"docs:dev": "vp run docs:assets && vp run docs:api:en && vp run @pantoken/components#generate && vp run @pantoken/plugin-stacking#generate && vp run @pantoken/plugin-transition#generate && vp run @pantoken/plugin-visual-debug#generate && vp run @pantoken/plugin-logos#generate && vp run @pantoken/plugin-primitives#generate && vp run docs:api:css && vitepress dev"
```
So the *startup* sequence is: stage demo assets (`docs:assets` → `docs/scripts/demos.ts`), build the English TypeDoc API, run each package's `generate` (tokens/component/plugin CSS), build the CSS-API markdown pages (`docs:api:css` → `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`), then start `vitepress dev`. Everything after startup is handled live by the orchestrator wired into the VitePress Vite config.

### 2. VitePress config and plugins

Config: **`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/.vitepress/config.ts`** (457 lines).

Vite plugins registered under `vite.plugins` (lines 359–381): the **`orchestrator`** (the workspace orchestrator, `apply: "serve"`) and `vitepress-plugin-llms`. Markdown-it plugins (lines 404–439): `mermaidPlugin`, `tokenValuePreview`, and **`demoMarkdownIt`** from `@pantoken/demo` (the live-demo runner). The theme lives in `docs/.vitepress/theme/` (`index.ts` imports the generated CSS — see section 4).

### 3. The orchestrator with direct `node` builds (the documented constraint)

The orchestrator package is **`@pantoken/vite-workspace-orchestrator`** at `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/plugins/vite/workspace-orchestrator/`:
- `src/index.ts` — the Vite plugin (`workspaceOrchestrator`). Watches each upstream `watchPaths` with native `fs.watch` (recursive), applies include/ignore glob filters (`matchesFilters`), and debounces (default 200 ms). Separately watches `outputWatchPaths` and bridges changes into Vite by calling `server.watcher.emit("change", …)` — CSS files already in the module graph get targeted HMR, everything else a full reload. Uses native `fs.watch` deliberately because chokidar filters paths outside the project root and doesn't observe pnpm-symlinked/out-of-root dirs.
- `src/scheduler.ts` — `createScheduler`. On a debounced change it `spawn`s the node's `build` command (`stdio: "inherit"`, `cwd: node.dir`), tracks building/pending state, and on success cascades to `dependents` in topological order.
- `src/types.ts` — `UpstreamNode` / `OrchestratorOptions` / `FileServerEntry`.
- `src/file-server.ts` — optional static middleware (not used by the docs config; no `fileServers` passed).

The constraint is documented in **`docs/.vitepress/config.ts` lines 15–29**:
> Builds invoke each package's `node` script DIRECTLY, not `vp run …`. `vpr docs:dev` runs vitepress under `vp`, and vite-plus cannot spawn a nested `vp` from inside that process — it dies with "Failed to spawn process: os error 22". A direct `node` invocation is unaffected. … NOTE: `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle needs `vp pack`, which likewise can't run nested, so it is NOT auto-rebuilt here.

The wired orchestrator (lines 30–64) has three upstream nodes, all using direct `node` builds:

| name | dir | watchPaths | build | dependents |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@pantoken/css` | `formats/css` | `formats/css/src` | `["node", "scripts/generate.ts"]` | — |
| `@pantoken/components` | `formats/components` | `formats/components/src` | `["node", "scripts/generate.ts"]` | `@pantoken/docs#docs:api:css` |
| `@pantoken/docs#docs:api:css` | `docs` | `cssdoc.json` | `["node", "scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` | — |

`outputWatchPaths`: `formats/css/generated`, `formats/components/generated`, `renderers/web-components/dist`.

So on a source edit: the package's `node scripts/generate.ts` regenerates its `generated/*.css`; the `outputWatchPaths` watcher bridges that into HMR; a components edit additionally cascades into `docs:api:css` which rebuilds the CSS-API `.md` pages (VitePress watches those emitted files itself). Web-components `dist` is only watched — it's rebuilt manually in a separate top-level shell because `vp pack` can't run nested.

### 4. Component CSS pipeline (src/components/*.css → docs demos)

Authoring → shipped chain in `formats/components`:
1. **Authoring source**: `src/components/*.css` (plus `src/utilities/*.css`, `src/rules/*.css`) — real CSS carrying a `PFX-` prefix sentinel and cssdoc `/** */` doc comments.
2. **`scripts/component-styles.ts`** compiles all those `.css` files into one TS module of per-theme string constants, `src/generated/component-styles.ts` (runs `themeCustomMedia` per theme rebrand/canvas/canvasHighContrast). This is the `?raw` workaround: `vp pack` (rolldown) can't resolve Vite's `?raw`, so the CSS text is baked into a `.ts` module. Doc comments are retained because `build-css-api.ts` later parses them.
3. **Record wrappers** (`src/components/alert.ts`, etc.) `import { alert as alertRaw } from "../generated/component-styles.ts"` and apply the prefix via `alertRaw.replaceAll(SENTINEL, p)`.

## Context

Editing `formats/components/src/components/billboard.css` while `vpr docs:dev` is running does **not**
show up in the browser — the demo/preview keeps the old style. The user wants the full transform
pipeline to run on save so a change like `border-color: var(--instui-component-link-text-color)` →
`border-color: red` (inside `@media (--theme-canvas)`) becomes a live red border on refresh.

Three things are broken in the dev watch chain:

1. **The docs multi-theme sheet is built from stale `dist`.** The sheet that actually styles the
   inline `@example` previews and the `/play` demos is the docs-only *multi-theme* sheet written by
   `docs/scripts/components-sheet.ts` → `scopedComponentsCss()` in
   [scope-components.ts](docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts). That function imports `componentsCss`
   from `@pantoken/components`, which resolves to `formats/components/dist/index.mjs` (confirmed — no
   `source`/`development` export condition, so vp's node resolves to `dist`). `dist` is only rebuilt by
   `vp pack`, which **cannot run nested** under `vpr docs:dev` ("Failed to spawn process: os error 22" —
   the same constraint the config comment already calls out for web-components). So no `src` edit ever
   reaches this sheet during dev. **This is the root cause** — the theme-conditional `--theme-canvas`
   rule the user is editing lives *only* in this sheet (the shipped rebrand `components.css` prunes it).

2. **`component-styles.ts` never re-runs on watch.** The `.css` authoring files are compiled into
   `src/generated/component-styles.ts` (the per-theme string module every record imports) by
   [component-styles.ts](formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts). The orchestrator's
   `@pantoken/components` node runs only `scripts/generate.ts`, which *consumes* that module but never
   regenerates it. So even the shipped `generated/components.css` (which feeds the CSS-API `.md` page
   text) is built from a stale module on a `.css` edit.

3. **`components-sheet.ts` isn't wired into the orchestrator at all.** Its own docstring claims "the
   config's workspace orchestrator invokes this script directly" on component edits, but nothing in
   [config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) invokes it. It runs one-shot at startup via
   `docs:assets` → `demos.ts` only.

## Fix

### 1. Read the docs multi-theme sheet from source, not `dist`

In [docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts](docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts), change the import:

```ts
// from:
import { componentsCss } from "@pantoken/components";
// to (matches the precedent in formats/components/scripts/generate.ts, which imports "../src/index.ts"):
import { componentsCss } from "../../../formats/components/src/index.ts";
```

This makes the multi-theme sheet reflect the freshly-regenerated `src/generated/component-styles.ts`
instead of the stale `dist` bundle — sidestepping the `vp pack` nested-spawn constraint entirely. It's
a build-time docs script (never shipped to the browser), so importing components' TS source is safe and
is actually *more* correct: the docs always render current source. Output is byte-identical to the
`dist`-sourced path once the module is fresh, preserving the "byte-for-byte the shipped sheet" claim in
[theme/index.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts).

### 2. Wire the full transform chain into the orchestrator

In [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts), replace the single `@pantoken/components`
upstream node with a chain that runs **component-styles → generate → components-sheet → docs:api:css**.
Model it with existing scripts (no new files) as two nodes for the components package plus one new
docs node:

```ts
{
  name: "@pantoken/components#styles",
  dir: at("formats/components"),
  watchPaths: [at("formats/components/src")],
  // Loop guard: component-styles.ts rewrites src/generated/component-styles.ts (plain writeFileSync,
  // always), and generate.ts rewrites src/generated/_records.css — both under the watched src dir.
  // Without this the recompile retriggers itself forever.
  ignore: ["generated/**"],
  build: ["node", "scripts/component-styles.ts"],
  dependents: ["@pantoken/components"],
},
{
  name: "@pantoken/components",
  dir: at("formats/components"),
  watchPaths: [],                       // dependent-only; scheduler resolves it by name
  build: ["node", "scripts/generate.ts"],
  dependents: ["@pantoken/docs#components-sheet", "@pantoken/docs#docs:api:css"],
},
{
  name: "@pantoken/docs#components-sheet",
  dir: at("docs"),
  watchPaths: [],
  build: ["node", "scripts/components-sheet.ts"],   // already runnable directly (self-run guard exists)
  dependents: [],
},
```

`#styles` (recompile byTheme module) → `@pantoken/components` (generate shipped sheets) →
[`components-sheet`](docs/scripts/components-sheet.ts) (rewrite the multi-theme sheet) +

Fix the now-accurate docstring in [components-sheet.ts](docs/scripts/components-sheet.ts) lines 19–22

required, but verify the wording matches the new wiring).

- [docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts](docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts) — root-cause import swap.
- [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) — orchestrator `upstream` graph (lines 30–64).
- Reused as-is: [component-styles.ts](formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts),
  [generate.ts](formats/components/scripts/generate.ts),
  [components-sheet.ts](docs/scripts/components-sheet.ts).

## Verification

1. Start the docs server on a distinct port (never reuse the user's):
   `vpr @pantoken/docs#docs:dev -- --port 5199 --strictPort` (or run the root `vpr docs:dev` if no

4. Watch the dev-server console: expect the orchestrator cascade to log

5. Confirm the browser shows a red hover border **without a manual rebuild** (a refresh is fine;

6. Guard against a watch loop: after the edit settles, confirm the console goes quiet (no repeating

7. Regression: `vpr docs:build` still succeeds (the source import must resolve under a production docs

## Scope boundary

This covers component / utility / rule edits under `formats/components/src` (everything
`componentsCss` aggregates). Edits to `base.css` / `prose.css` / `icons.css` / stand-alone
`utilities.css` served to `/play` still read from `dist` copies staged by `demos.ts` and won't live-

Three things are broken in the dev watch chain:

1. **The docs multi-theme sheet is built from stale `dist`.** The sheet that actually styles the
   inline `@example` previews and the `/play` demos is the docs-only *multi-theme* sheet written by

   [scope-components.ts](docs/scripts/lib/scope-components.ts). That function imports `componentsCss`
   from `@pantoken/components`, which resolves to `formats/components/dist/index.mjs` (confirmed — no
   `source`/`development` export condition, so vp's node resolves to `dist`). `dist` is only rebuilt by
   `vp pack`, which **cannot run nested** under `vpr docs:dev` ("Failed to spawn process: os error 22" —
   the same constraint the config comment already calls out for web-components). So no `src` edit ever
   reaches this sheet during dev. **This is the root cause** — the theme-conditional `--theme-canvas`
   rule the user is editing lives *only* in this sheet (the shipped rebrand `components.css` prunes it).

2. **`component-styles.ts` never re-runs on watch.** The `.css` authoring files are compiled into
   `src/generated/component-styles.ts` (the per-theme string module every record imports) by
   [component-styles.ts](formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts). The orchestrator's
   `@pantoken/components` node runs only `scripts/generate.ts`, which *consumes* that module but never
   regenerates it. So even the shipped `generated/components.css` (which feeds the CSS-API `.md` page
   text) is built from a stale module on a `.css` edit.

3. **`components-sheet.ts` isn't wired into the orchestrator at all.** Its own docstring claims "the
   config's workspace orchestrator invokes this script directly" on component edits, but nothing in
   [config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) invokes it. It runs one-shot at startup via

Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside** that process — e.g. the `@pantoken/vite-workspace-orchestrator` plugin's rebuild `spawn()` — dies with `✗ Failed to spawn process: underlying os error: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on cache-miss (the real worker spawn; cache-hit replay is fine, which is why it looks intermittent). So `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`'s orchestrator `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package dir), NOT `["pnpm","exec","vp","run","X#build"]`. The theme imports only *generated CSS* from `@pantoken/css` + `@pantoken/components`, so their `generate` scripts suffice (no `vp pack` needed). The CSS API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`), watches root `cssdoc.json`, and is a `dependent` of `@pantoken/components` (component edit → regen sheet → rebuild docs). VitePress watches the emitted `docs/api/**/*.md` itself, so no HMR wiring needed for the pages.

CASUALTY: `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (dist JS the theme imports), which also can't nest — so it's NOT in the live orchestrator. Rebuild it manually in a separate top-level shell (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `reloadWatchPaths` on its `dist` then bridges the change into HMR. Its shadow-CSS still reaches the docs (build-css-api reads the `.css` sources directly).

The `vp run X && vp run Y` chain *inside* the `docs:dev` package.json script works fine — that's a different (top-level script-runner) context, not a spawn from within the running vitepress process. See [[cssdoc-system]], [[web-components-css-tooling]].

Done. Web components and every remaining demo/`@example` surface now live-reload during `vpr docs:dev`. The unifying trick throughout: import package **source** (not `dist`) wherever the docs would otherwise need the nested-forbidden `vp pack`.

## What changed

**Web components** — [docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts) now imports `register()` from `renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` (source). That graph is Node-free and needs no codegen — element CSS comes via Vite `?inline` + `@pantoken/components` `*Css()` — so Vite hot-reloads element `.ts` and co-located `.css` edits directly, no `vp pack`, no orchestrator node. `register()` is idempotent, so the source barrel's load-time call is safe. Dropped the now-unused `renderers/web-components/dist` from `outputWatchPaths`.

**Plugin decoration sheets + focus-outline** — new [stage-plugin-assets.ts](docs/scripts/stage-plugin-assets.ts) copies the transition/stacking/visual-debug `generated/*.css` into `demos-assets`; [stage-component-assets.ts](docs/scripts/stage-component-assets.ts) now also writes `focus-outline.css` from source. [demos.ts](docs/scripts/demos.ts) drops the stale `dist`-function computations.

**Plugin `@example` pages (all 5)** — [config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) gains a watch→`node scripts/generate.ts` node per plugin (writes a `generated/` sibling of `src`, so no loop), cascading to `docs:api:css` (+ `plugin-assets` for the three with demo sheets).

**docs/demos/*.html snippets** — new [stage-demo-snippets.ts](docs/scripts/stage-demo-snippets.ts) + a watch node on `docs/demos`.

**Token / site-themes sheet** — [site-themes.ts](docs/scripts/site-themes.ts) imports `toCss`/`byTheme`/`themes` from `formats/{css,tokens}/src` and mirrors into `demos-assets`; a new `#site-themes` node watches `formats/tokens/generated` and is a dependent of `@pantoken/css`.

**Ordering** — [docs/package.json](docs/package.json) `docs:dev` runs all package `#generate` before `docs:assets`.

## Verified live (each edit → observed effect, then reverted)

- **Web component**: edited `web-components/src/elements/tooltip.css` → Vite `page reload` of the source file, no errors, elements registered from source.
- **Plugin sheet**: `transition/src` `300ms→321ms` → cascade `plugin-transition → [plugin-assets, docs:api:css]`, served `demos-assets/transition.css` showed `321ms`.
- **Demo snippet**: edited `docs/demos/base.html` → `demo-snippets` node re-copied, served `/demos/base.html` reflected it.
- **Token value**: flipped a token in `rebrand.json` → `#site-themes` node rebuilt → `hmr update .../site-themes.css`, value present in both the theme import and the `/play` copy.

Working tree holds only the intended source changes; all probe edits are reverted.

One boundary remains by nature: the TypeDoc-generated `@example` **page markup** (the code text on web-component API pages) rebuilds at startup only — editing an element's *behavior/CSS* is live, but changing the `@example` HTML in a TSDoc comment needs a restart. Wiring TypeDoc into the cascade is possible if you want that too.

Done. TypeDoc `@example` markup now regenerates live too.

## What changed

- **New [docs/scripts/build-api-en.ts](docs/scripts/build-api-en.ts)** — the `docs:api:en` chain (TypeDoc + badge styling + overview page) as a single `node`-invocable script. It spawns TypeDoc as a plain `node <bin>` (resolved via `typedoc/package.json`), so the nested-`vp` limit doesn't apply, and the orchestrator's single-argv `build` can call it.
- **[docs/package.json](docs/package.json)** — `docs:api:en` now just runs that wrapper (single source of truth for startup and the watch node).
- **[docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts)** — new `@pantoken/docs#api:en` node that rebuilds the API pages on a TS edit. Scoped to the **renderer** sources (`include: ["**/src/**/*.ts", "**/src/**/*.tsx"]`, ignoring dist/generated), because TypeDoc reparses the whole entry-point set on every run — a broader watch would make every component/plugin/token save pay for a full-monorepo TypeDoc and slow the fast loops I built earlier. VitePress watches the emitted `docs/api/**/*.md`, so no extra HMR wiring.

## Verified live

Edited the `@example` in [badge.ts](renderers/web-components/src/elements/badge.ts) (`9` → `42`), saved: the `api:en` node ran (`building → done`, ~4s), `hmr update .../variables/badge.md` fired, and the page updated with no restart — both the **rendered example** (`instui-badge` showing `42`) and the **displayed code block** (`<instui-badge variant="danger">42</instui-badge>`). Reverted; tree is clean (only the intended source changes remain; `billboard.css` was already modified at session start).

## The scope boundary, now closed

Editing a renderer element — its behavior, co-located CSS, *or* its TSDoc `@example` markup — is fully live. The one deliberate limit: `@example` edits in **non-renderer** packages (e.g. a `formats/*` or `plugins/*` TSDoc block) still need a restart to re-render their API-page markup, since I kept the TypeDoc watch narrow to protect dev-loop speed. Widening it is a one-line `watchPaths` addition (point it at `formats`, `plugins`, etc.) if you decide the tradeoff is worth it — say the word.

## What

Make everything with a local demo or native `@example` hot-reload on a source edit under `vpr docs:dev`. Previously, editing a component/plugin/token/web-component source did **not** show up in the browser: the docs previews and `/play` demos loaded package `dist`, which is only rebuilt by `vp pack` — and `vp pack` can't run nested under `vpr docs:dev`.

## How

The unifying fix: read package **source** (not `dist`) wherever the docs would otherwise need a nested `vp pack`, and wire the workspace orchestrator to regenerate + re-stage on the matching source edit.

- **Component sheets** — the multi-theme sheet and the base/prose/icons/select/utilities + focus-outline demo assets are sourced from `formats/components` src/`generated`, with a `component-styles → generate → components-sheet + component-assets + docs:api:css` cascade.
- **Plugin sheets** — one watch→`node scripts/generate.ts` node per plugin (transition/stacking/visual-debug/logos/primitives); the three decoration sheets re-stage into `demos-assets`, and all five rebuild their CSS-API `@example` pages.
- **Web components** — the theme imports `register()` from the web-components **source** (Node-free, codegen-free; Vite hot-reloads element `.ts` + co-located `.css` directly). `register()` is idempotent, so the source barrel's load-time call is safe.
- **Tokens** — `site-themes.ts` imports `toCss`/`byTheme`/`themes` from source; a `#site-themes` node watches the token IR and is a dependent of `@pantoken/css`.
- **Demo snippets** — `docs/demos/*.html` re-copy on edit.
- **TypeDoc `@example`** — a `node`-invocable API build (`build-api-en.ts`) lets a `#api:en` node rebuild the API pages on renderer source edits, so element `@example` markup goes live. Scoped to renderer sources to keep the other fast loops from paying for a full-monorepo TypeDoc.
- **Startup order** — `docs:dev` runs all package `#generate` before `docs:assets`.

## Verification

Each surface was verified live in the dev server (edit → observed effect in the browser/served asset, then reverted): a `--theme-canvas` billboard rule, a `base.css` value, a utility/icon sheet, a plugin duration token (`transition`), a `docs/demos/*.html` snippet, a token IR value (`site-themes` HMR), a web-component co-located CSS edit, and a web-component TSDoc `@example` (`badge`, both the rendered example and the code block updated). No watch loops observed; the type-check passes via the pre-commit hook.
